pilgrimage

PIL-grim-ij — a pilgrimage is the journey a 'pilgrim' takes, usually for religious or deeply personal reasons. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pilgrimage is a religious or spiritual journey, often to a sacred place.

Every year, thousands of believers undertake a pilgrimage to the ancient temple on the mountain.

Example

A woman spends her entire life savings and six weeks on a pilgrimage, walking hundreds of miles across a foreign country and visiting sacred sites along the way, in order to fulfill a lifelong spiritual goal she has held since childhood.

That long, deeply meaningful journey undertaken for spiritual reasons is what makes it a pilgrimage. Unlike 'vacation,' which is for rest and enjoyment, pilgrimage is undertaken specifically for religious or spiritual purpose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

spiritual journey: A spiritual journey is any experience of inner religious or personal growth, and it needs no travel at all -- it can happen entirely at home. A pilgrimage is the physical version: an actual trip, usually to a sacred place, undertaken for exactly that spiritual purpose.

expedition: An expedition is a journey organized for exploration, research, or a concrete mission -- mapping a coastline, reaching a pole, collecting specimens. A pilgrimage is organized around devotion instead: the traveler goes to a sacred place to fulfill a spiritual purpose, not to bring back findings.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

casual outing: a short, relaxed trip with no deeper purpose

errand: a short, practical task or trip

Where it sits · how purposeful the journey is

trek → pilgrimage → quest

trek vs. pilgrimage: A trek is less purposeful than a pilgrimage and more about physical difficulty: a long, exhausting journey, often on foot, taken for adventure or exercise as easily as for faith. A pilgrimage is defined by its destination and sacred purpose -- even a comfortable train ride to a shrine can be a pilgrimage, but never a trek.

quest vs. pilgrimage: Quest can feel broader than pilgrimage: pilgrimage is always a physical journey to a sacred place, while quest can describe any determined pursuit, physical or not.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — peregr-: foreign, traveling abroad (Latin (peregrinus, from per- + ager, 'through the field/land'))

Put it together: Latin peregrinus meant 'foreigner, one traveling abroad,' built from per- ('through') and ager ('field, land'). A pilgrimage is, at its root, a journey through foreign land undertaken for a meaningful purpose.

Use the root in a new word: peregrine: The peregrine falcon is famous for traveling incredible distances during its yearly migration.
